essay.q: Explain why Venkatesh et al. (2003) needed to unify the eight technology acceptance models: name the eight models, the number of constructs, the four moderators, and the five limits of earlier comparison studies with how the paper addresses them.
essay.m: Hint: Many competing models (typically over 40% of intention variance), forcing "pick and choose". Eight: TRA, TAM, MM, TPB, C-TAM-TPB, MPCU, IDT, SCT; 32 constructs; moderators: experience, voluntariness, gender, age. Five limits: simple technologies, student participants, late retrospective measurement, cross-sectional or between-subject designs, voluntary contexts; addressed by organizational technologies, employees, tracking from introduction, longitudinal within-person design, both voluntary and mandatory settings.

essay.q: Describe the design and main results of the empirical comparison of the eight models (four organizations, three measurements, usage logs), including the three consistent findings that led to UTAUT.
essay.m: Hint: Four organizations (entertainment, telecommunications, banking, public administration), N = 119 voluntary and 96 mandatory; T1, T2, T3; usage logs over six months; PLS with 500 bootstraps. Results: intention variance 17% to 42%; three findings: each model has a stable strongest construct (attitude, usefulness, extrinsic motivation, job-fit, relative advantage, outcome expectations); some constructs lose significance over time (behavioral control, ease of use, complexity, self-efficacy, anxiety); social constructs are significant only in mandatory settings.

essay.q: Present UTAUT: the four core constructs (definitions and the original constructs merged), the four moderators and hypotheses H1 to H6. Explain why attitude, self-efficacy and anxiety are not direct determinants.
essay.m: Hint: Performance expectancy (usefulness, extrinsic motivation, job-fit, relative advantage, outcome expectations); effort expectancy (ease of use, complexity, IDT ease of use); social influence (subjective norm, social factors, image); facilitating conditions (behavioral control, facilitating conditions, compatibility). H1 to H6 and moderation. Attitude is significant only when performance and effort expectancy are absent, so the relation is spurious; self-efficacy and anxiety act through effort expectancy (Venkatesh 2000); facilitating conditions are captured by effort expectancy for intention but affect use directly.

essay.q: Analyze the role of the moderators (gender, age, experience, voluntariness) in UTAUT and the interaction results for each construct; state the limits in interpreting the interactions.
essay.m: Hint: Performance expectancy: three-way interaction, salient for men and younger workers; effort expectancy: women, older workers, early stages; social influence: mandatory, women, older, early stages (four-way); facilitating conditions for use: older workers, growing experience. Explained via gender roles and socialization; limits: main effects are not interpretable with higher-order interactions; 24 cells need adequate representation; "nonsignificant" results have low power for small effects; underlying mechanisms need study.

essay.q: Evaluate the validation results of UTAUT (initial test and cross-validation): R² and adjusted R² for direct effects versus interactions, and the limits of the evidence.
essay.m: Hint: Initial test N = 215: R² direct only .40, .41, .42; with interactions .51, .52, .50; pooled N = 645: .31 and .76, adj. .27 and .69. Cross-validation N = 133 (voluntary N = 80, mandatory N = 53): similar, pooled adj. with interactions .70. Limits: scales pruned to highest-loading items, intention as main outcome, no link to outcomes, sparse moderator cells, pooling with repeated measures, possibly near the limit of explanation; not evidence about AI or learning.

essay.q: Propose how to use UTAUT for a thesis on AI teaching programming, marking design inference and what must be added beyond UTAUT.
essay.m: Hint (design inference): four factors: performance expectancy (AI helps me learn programming), effort expectancy, social influence (instructors, peers; measure perceived voluntariness), facilitating conditions (tools, support); measure at several times (start, middle, end of term) because effort expectancy fades with experience; rewrite and validate scales (especially content validity); consider moderators in a student sample with a narrow age range. Add: appropriate reliance (Module 10) and learning outcomes without AI, because UTAUT does not link to outcomes.
